alternatives.name: Prefect
alternatives.why_not_default: No supplied or scheduled flow was executed in the retained review. Process containment, cancellation and checkpoint recovery remain unqualified; adoption also requires a persistent server/database and worker lifecycle.

alternatives.name: Dagster
alternatives.why_not_default: Partitioned assets and backfill lineage could justify adoption, but application definitions are absent and no execution establishes this layer's cancellation, containment or recovery contract.

alternatives.name: Restate
alternatives.why_not_default: Retained evidence is source review, with no executed workload recovery comparison. Adding persistence, authentication and SDK operations has no demonstrated benefit for the selected local workflows.

alternatives.name: Temporal
alternatives.why_not_default: Cross-host durability could justify escalation, but no retained executed comparison establishes better recovery for this workload. Production persistence, visibility, authentication and upgrade operations add unmeasured burden.

limits: This review inspected retained local records; it did not rerun native workloads or independently inspect the complete hosted guest archive.
Current upstream releases and behavior beyond the retained revisions were not verified.
No executed head-to-head scheduler comparison was present in the reviewed evidence.
open_gaps: Physical-host failure, power loss, independent-host recovery and arbitrary production effects remain unqualified.
Local process termination does not establish remote provider cancellation, billing cessation or distributed exactly-once effects.
The orderly reboot experiment uses a synthetic workload; its project oracle is separate from the selected unchanged upstream Dagu retry tests.
Persistent manual history and one guest timer do not establish every production schedule or daemon policy.
The retained foundation review leaves the next genuine daily maintenance trigger and restart persistence unobserved.

arms: Dagu plus systemd using the retained cancellation, checkpoint, history and containment protocols
One of Prefect, Dagster, Restate or Temporal implementing the same workload and effect contract, with process supervision where needed
overturn_protocol.metric: Preserved run history; cancellation and process-tree cleanup within declared bounds; unchanged checkpoint with one execution; same-run successful recovery and one completed local effect; independent recovery observation; deployment and operating burden.

overturn_when: Reopen if the selected deployment fails the acceptance in blueprints/convergence-practice/job-recovery/plan.json, blueprints/convergence-practice/service-reboot/plan.json or the supervised blueprints/us-equities/worker-supervision/fixture.py, and an executed challenger comparison passes the same contract with acceptable operating burden. Freeze any additional host-loss or external-effect acceptance before comparing it.
why_selected: Dagu and systemd provide complementary, retained native execution evidence. blueprints/us-equities/hosting/receipt.json records failed and cancelled Dagu runs and preserved history after service restart. blueprints/us-equities/worker-supervision/README.md records deadline termination of a TERM-ignoring parent and descendants, verified absent by PID/starttime, followed by a successful fresh run. blueprints/convergence-practice/job-recovery/README.md records cancellation and selected-step retry with an unchanged checkpoint on Mac and WSL. evidence/receipts/native-service-reboot-20260920.json records independently observed same-run recovery after one orderly guest reboot with one local effect. These establish bounded native behavior through local integration workloads, including synthetic fixtures, rather than general disaster recovery.
